author: Ifmyante
text:
Everybody here is welcome to come and go as we please.

This is a pleasant community, filled with mutual respect and
camaraderie. We have some absolutely amazing traders and analysts here,
and we'd like to keep them coming back.

So please everybody, stick to the rules of the forum, and don't pester other users, in the threads or via PM.

If you have questions, try hard to work the answers out yourself (as
this is the ultimate way to learn), and if you get stuck, post them
either in the place they arose, or your journal, or the classroom.

Let's keep this place lovely for everybody

Thanks

author: haanz
text:
Yes, it's true to learn with fun, and start from the basic. I used to
received some PM, and I PM salivan for guideline on how to learn from
this forum in the fastest way as this forum is big, but in the end i
figure out we just have to navigate around coz everything is here, and
start from the pieces, go through them one by one.

Dont put too much pressure to become successfully quick, it's not that
way, and it wont work, because if we put too much pressure on ourselves
to meet the timeline, we eventually lose our patience, and become too
emotion in every trade we take. The worst part is we don't find the best
 setup to trade, and simply go in even the setup is ugly, and not clear
for the entry, eventually will make your trade worse.

Until recently i realise all of these, and totally stop the trading.
Practice from one section to another, while in the process, just enjoy
the fun part, why it works, and why it doesn't. Find out the reasons
why, and how to improve. Take it slow and steady. Without the pressure, I
 find it learning with more fun and I progress faster than I expected.
There are so many section in this forum we can learn, the mistakes and
AHA moment from the seniors. Along the way, we progress and become a
better trader.

Enjoy learning hope everyone progress well here.

Ohya, by the way, roadmap is an excellent guide to follow the learning
path. Start from basic then progress, try not to find a short cut.

author: Ifmyante
text:
I've been accused at times of giving "cryptic answers" to questions here, and I've noticed other great analysts have too.

The thing is, when I read someone else's short reply to a long question,
 I usually tend to think "you've hit the nail right on the head there!
You didn't need to say another word!"

I defy anybody who thinks they've been dismissed by one of these
answers, to log them, and come back to them months later. I can almost
guarantee that you'll read it and think "chuff, that was a brilliant
answer!"

The greatest mentors are those who help you reach your own enlightenment, because enlightenment can't be given
